meta.note: Locked mahjong terms. One form per language per term, decided once with a native speaker. A translation that renders a locked term differently is a CI failure, not a style preference. English forms are filled; all other core locales are explicitly null (untranslated) in Phase 1 — do NOT invent or machine-translate them. The call/noun family is split into separate locked terms (pon = the call, pung = the triplet noun) and the MCR pattern names are locked as their own entries, because no single form can express them — see the research annotations and ~/workspace/mahjong-prep/pung-pon-research.md.

bot.note: The CPU opponent. Never 'AI' — in every locale, the opponent is always called Bot.

fu.note: Mini-points: the base value of a hand before han are applied.

han.note: Scoring unit (doubling unit); one han doubles the hand value.

honba.note: Repeat counter: extra hands the same dealer deals after winning.

pon.note: The call: the word shouted to claim a discard for a triplet (riichi). The triplet itself is the separate locked term pung. In American / MCR / Hong Kong / Taiwanese English the spoken claim is also 'Pung' — that word is locked under pung; this entry locks the riichi call.

research.note: Call/noun split applied Nov 20, 2026 (Michael approved the research proposal's structure; the forms themselves still await a native speaker): the noun forms that used to be annotated on this entry live on the pung entry. English uses Pon for the riichi call and Pung for the triplet noun in American / MCR / Hong Kong / Taiwanese copy — one locked English form cannot cover both; see research file, Structural finding.

pung.note: A three-of-a-kind meld (triplet) — the noun, in American / MCR / Hong Kong / Taiwanese copy. The call that claims a discard is the separate locked term pon (the riichi call; in the Pung variants the spoken claim is this same word).
